faqs.a: Complementary colors sit directly opposite on the color wheel — blue and orange, red and green. They create the strongest possible contrast, which is why they are used for call-to-action buttons and highlights.
Split-complementary uses the two colors adjacent to the direct complement (+/-150 degrees instead of 180). You keep strong contrast but with less visual tension — easier to use across a whole page.
For #4f46e5 (hue ~243 degrees), the complement sits at 63 degrees: a yellow-green around #e5dd48. Opposite hues always pair this way — the tool computes it exactly for your base color.
faqs.q: What is the complement of indigo #4f46e5?

faqs.a: Use the complement sparingly — for buttons, links and small accents. Large areas of two complements side by side can vibrate and tire the eyes. Split-complementary pairs are safer for bigger surfaces.
faqs.q: How do I use complements without hurting readability?

complementary-color.formula:
complement hue = (base hue + 180) mod 360
split-complementary hues = (base hue +/- 150) mod 360
saturation and lightness stay equal to the base color
howTo: Pick your base color or type its HEX code.
Read the complement (+180 degrees) and the two split-complementary colors (+/-150 degrees).
Preview all four as a gradient strip.
Click the copy button on any swatch to copy its HEX code.
Use complements for accents, buttons and highlights in your design.
keyFacts: A complement sits exactly 180 degrees away on the color wheel.
Split-complementary colors sit at +150 and -150 degrees.
Only the hue rotates; saturation and lightness match the base color.
Complementary pairs give the maximum possible hue contrast.
complementary-color.keywords: complementary color, opposite color, color wheel complement, split complementary, contrast colors
limitations: Maximum hue contrast does not guarantee readable text — check WCAG contrast separately.
Full-strength complements can vibrate when placed side by side in large areas.
Only hue is rotated; no lighter/darker variants are suggested.
Taste still matters — math finds the opposite, not the prettiest pair.

complementary-color.workedExample:
Take #4f46e5 with hue ~243.4 degrees, saturation 75.4%, lightness 58.6%.
Complement: (243.4 + 180) mod 360 = 63.4 degrees.
hsl(63.4, 75.4%, 58.6%): chroma C = 0.6235; x = 0.5882; m = 0.2745.
Sector 1 (60-120 deg): (x, c, 0) + m = (0.8627, 0.8980, 0.2745); x255 = (220.0, 229.0, 70.0), rounds to (220, 229, 70).
Result: #dce546 — a yellow-green, the exact complement of the indigo base.
